articles.title: Every NFL Team's Most Sensible Trade Asset Ahead of Week 4
articles.summary: The 2026 NFL trade deadline won't arrive until November 10, but the market is open for business and already seeing some noteworthy activity.
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline won't arrive until November 10, but the market is open for business and already seeing some noteworthy activity.

On Monday, the Minnesota Vikings traded quarterback J.J. McCarthy to the New York Giants. Late Wednesday evening, the Pittsburgh Steelers agreed to send cornerback Joey Porter Jr. to the Dallas Cowboys. We're going to see more trades over the next five weeks, and some of them may be significant.

Of course, not every team will be looking to move a marquee player or a premium position this early in the season. Some teams undoubtedly view themselves as deadline buyers, not sellers, as the season approaches its quarter mark. However, every franchise has at least one player who would be a sensible asset on the trade market.

Whether due to contract status, depth-chart positioning, or pure market value, the following players should be viewed as logical trade chips ahead of Week 4.

The Arizona Cardinals may want to try moving 2024 first-round pick and wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr., given his lack of development and the emergence of new No. 1 wideout Michael Wilson. However, at least one team believes that Harrison wouldn't garner more than a high Day 3 draft pick at this point, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler .

Giving up on Harrison for a fourth- or fifth-rounder wouldn't be very logical. The Cardinals are in the early stages of their latest rebuild, and Harrison could still become a long-term piece of their puzzle.

Safety Budda Baker, however, probably doesn't have a lengthy future in Arizona. The 30-year-old is still a starting-caliber safety, but he looms as a likely 2027 cap casualty.

The Cardinals could save $17.9 million in cap space by trading or releasing Baker in the offseason. With consecutive losses making a 2026 run seem unlikely, Arizona should start weighing Baker's value as a trade chip.

Tua Tagovailoa was a Pro Bowler with the Miami Dolphins in 2023, but he was released just two years later. He signed a one-year deal with the Atlanta Falcons in the offseason and was set to be Atlanta's Week 1 starter before he was sidelined by an oblique injury.

Of course, it's fair to wonder if Tagovailoa won the job by default. 2024 first-round pick Michael Penix Jr. was limited in camp while recovering from a torn ACL. Tagovailoa didn't perform particularly well in the preseason, and ProFootballTalk's Mike Florio reported in early September that there was a "strong possibility" that the quarterback could be cut if and when he was benched.

Tagovailoa was never benched, to be fair. He and Penix both got healthy in time for Week 3, and Penix got the start. Penix also played well in Atlanta's first win of the season, and it currently feels unlikely that he'll cede the QB1 role.

If the Falcons believe that Penix is ready to be "the guy" and can put them back in the playoff hunt, then Tagovailoa might be the most expendable player on the roster who actually has any trade value—Cooper Rush, who started and performed poorly in Weeks 1 and 2, probably does not.

The Baltimore Ravens are 2-1 under new head coach Jesse Minter and are probably far more interested in adding to their roster than breaking it down. If they need to move a player to make a deal, though, cornerback Chidobe Awuzie would be a logical trade chip.

Awuzie appeared in 14 games with the Ravens last season, and he re-signed on a one-year, $5 million deal with Baltimore in the offseason to again provide depth in the secondary. However, he hasn't done much of that through the first three weeks of the season.

The 31-year-old has appeared in all three games this season, but he's played a mere 22 defensive snaps and eight special-teams snaps. Trading him would save the Ravens $1.5 million in cap space.

49ers Owner Jed York Suspended 6 Games (AP)

In 2024, the Buffalo Bills used a fourth-round pick on Kentucky running back Ray Davis. The former Wildcat flashed some promise as a rookie, recording 631 scrimmage yards and six touchdowns, but he has since become a bigger contributor on special teams.

Davis was a first-team All-Pro punt returner in 2025.

The Bills could return Davis to a prominent backfield role by moving receiving back Ty Johnson, who is set to be a free agent in 2027. Johnson missed the first two games of the season with a hamstring injury but is healthy now and caught four passes for 50 yards in Week 3.

While Johnson does fill a valuable role in Buffalo's offense, Davis should be capable of taking over. Johnson could draw a solid trade return after the recent rash of running back injuries.

During the 2024 draft, the Carolina Panthers traded into the back end of Round 1 to select wide receiver Xavier Legette. Since then, though, Legette has struggled to establish himself as a reliable go-to receiver.

The 25-year-old has missed time this season with a knee injury, but he didn't exactly shine in his first two seasons. Through 33 career games, he has just 924 receiving yards and seven touchdowns. Meanwhile, 2025 first-round pick Tetairoa McMillan has established himself as Carolina's No. 1 receiver, while Jalen Coker has emerged as its No. 2.

The Panthers also just used a third-round pick on former Tennessee receiver Chris Brazzell II , though he's out for the season with a torn LCL.

While Legette isn't developing as expected in Carolina, he would undoubtedly interest other receiver-needy teams. He's battled drops (10) but is still a young 6'1", 221-pound pass-catcher with 4.39-second speed.

Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson wants his team to be an offensive powerhouse in 2026.

"We want to be the highest-scoring, we want to have the most wins, we want to win Super Bowls," Johnson said, per Steve Reed of the Associated Press.

Johnson probably won't want to part with any of his offensive stars, but tight end Cole Kmet should be viewed as a tradeable asset. Colston Loveland has taken over as TE1, and Kmet has just two receptions through three games this season. However, he's been a high-end producer in the past.

Kmet, who has three 500-yard seasons on his resume, should interest teams in need of a starting tight end.

Tight end Mike Gesicki has proven that he can be a difference-making piece of the Cincinnati Bengals' offense. However, he hasn't filled that role consistently. In Week 1, for example, he caught five passes for 78 yards and a touchdown. However, he had just three catches between Weeks 2 and 3 and finished 2025 with 307 yards.

Gesicki should be viewed as a viable trade chip by the Bengals. He's talented, but he's also 30 and will likely be a cap casualty in 2027.

The Bengals can save $8 million in 2027 cap space by releasing or trading Gesicki in the spring. They also have multiple other options at tight end in Drew Sample, Eric All Jr., Jack Endries, and Tanner Hudson.

Cleveland Browns receiver Jerry Jeudy had a trio of clutch catches during Thursday night's win over the Pittsburgh Steelers. However, he simply hasn't been a major part of the passing attack this season, as rookies K.C. Concepcion and Denzel Boston have taken over the receiver room.

Jeudy has just five catches on the season and had just one target and zero catches in Weeks 2 and 3.

With Concepcion, Boston, and tight end Harold Fannin Jr. representing Cleveland's future, Jeudy's time with the Browns could be coming to an end. However, he would interest receiver-needy teams, as he's a former Pro Bowler and 1,000-yard receiver who is still only 27 years old.

Jeudy's $1.5 million base salary would also appeal to teams on a budget.

The Cowboys' move to acquire Porter has made it very clear that Dallas is looking to chase the playoffs in 2026, and it was exactly the sort of move that franchise owner Jerry Jones hinted at before the start of the offseason.

"You look at it generally speaking, we're in play," Jones told 105.3 The Fan ahead of Week 1 (h/t Tommy Yarrish of the team's official website). "...You could look for it to be defensively."

The Cowboys are unlikely to move any players they believe are critical to this season's success. However, they could look to move a minor role players like tight end Luke Schoonmaker.

The 2023 second-round pick simply hasn't established himself as a key piece of the offensive puzzle and is firmly behind Jake Ferguson on the depth chart. He has just 459 receiving yards in 54 games and has never played more than 35 percent of the offensive snaps in a season. However, Ferguson is still a 28-year-old former Day-2 pick who should interest tight end-needy teams.

Following their Week 1 flop, the Denver Broncos have looked like legitimate title contenders in each of the past two weeks. They probably aren't very interested in moving key contributors right now. If they can get something in exchange for receiver/returner Marvin Mims Jr., though, they'd have to consider it.

Mims was an All-Pro returner in 2024, and he won't even turn 25 until March. However, it's still hard to envision him being a major piece of Denver's long-term puzzle. He's missed the last two games with a foot injury, and Denver has gotten by just fine with undrafted rookie Kolbe Katsis returning punts.

And the Broncos don't have a clear offensive role for Mims, who will be a free agent in the spring. Mims has just 1,202 career receiving yards, and the acquisition of Jaylen Waddle likely pushed him to the bottom of a depth chart that also features Courtland Sutton, Pat Bryant, and Troy Franklin.

The Detroit Lions are 2-1, but their defense has been an issue through the first three weeks. While trading away a rotational defensive lineman may seem counterintuitive, Levi Onwuzurike has already been deemed expendable once.

The Lions released Onwuzurike in early September before re-signing him to the practice squad and, eventually, the active roster. He has appeared in two games this season but has only played 33 defensive snaps.

If Detroit could move Onwuzurike as part of a package for secondary help, it should consider it. The 28-year-old missed all of last season with a torn ACL but should interest teams with needs along the defensive front. He appeared in 16 games with 10 starts in 2024 and recorded 28 tackles and 1.5 sacks that season.

Green Bay Packers: CB Carrington Valentine

The Green Bay Packers have made three straight trips to the postseason. However, they are now looking to overcome a 1-2 start to the season, and they're unlikely to move any of their full-time players at this point of the campaign.

Cornerback Carrington Valentine was a full-time player for most of last season, but he isn't now. Rookie second-round pick Brandon Cisse earned the starting job opposite Keisean Nixon in camp and has relegated Valentine to a reserve role.

Valentine has appeared in two games this season but has played just 18 defensive snaps. He's also set to be a free agent in 2026 and could be viewed as expendable.

While the Packers may not place much value on Valentine right now, other teams might. He has 51 games and 30 starts on his resume and is still only 25 years old.

The Houston Texans are 0-3, but you can bet that they're not ready to give up on the season or fire-sell starting talent. Houston started last season 0-3, too, and it still went on to reach the divisional round.

The Texans could, however, consider moving off of depth pieces while trying to address other areas of need. Center Jake Andrews is a former starter who is now backing up free-agent addition Evan Brown.

Andrews has played just 12 special-teams snaps this season, but he started 16 games in 2025 and made one start for the New England Patriots in 2023. With centers like Jovaughn Gwyn and Elgton Jenkins already suffering injuries, Andrews should have some early-season trade value.

Indianapolis Colts: QB Anthony Richardson

Anthony Richardson was the fourth overall pick in the 2023 draft, and for a brief window, he was the Indianapolis Colts' quarterback of the future. However, Indianapolis was prepared to turn the page by his third season and has since committed to Daniel Jones at quarterback.

This offseason, Richardson had to battle 2025 sixth-round pick Riley Leonard just to earn the backup role.

Richardson is the back, and according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , the Colts don't want to trade him right now. However, he's set to be a free agent in 2027 after having his fifth-year option declined, and Indy should explore cashing him in now.

While Richardson's trade value has undoubtedly fallen over the last few years, he should interest teams that don't have a clear quarterback plan beyond 2027. We've seen several signal-callers recently find success in their second acts, and Richardson's physical upside remains extremely high.

The Jacksonville Jaguars traded for offensive tackle Cole Van Lanen back in 2022, though he didn't step in and take over at offensive tackle until last season. In the spring, Jacksonville signed him to a three-year, $51 million extension.

With Anton Harrison manning Trevor Lawrence's blind side and Van Lanen opposite him, former starter Walker Little has become a pure depth piece. Trading him would save the Jags $11.4 million in cap space.

In addition to some valuable cap flexibility, the Jaguars could also expect to get a reasonable return for Little. He has played just 40 total snaps on offense and special teams this season but has made 39 starts in his career.

With tackles like Braxton Jones, Fred Johnson, and Josh Simmons already suffering injuries in the early season, offensive tackles will likely be in demand in the coming weeks.

Kansas City Chiefs: Edge Felix Anudike-Uzomah

At 3-0, the Kansas City Chiefs probably aren't looking to part with any key contributors. However, they might be able to get a reasonable return for part-time edge-defender Felix Anudike-Uzomah.

The 2023 first-round pick has never developed into the centerpiece defender the Chiefs hoped he could be. He made just three starts over his first two seasons, missed Year 3 with a hamstring injury, and had his fifth-year option declined by Kansas City. While Anudike-Uzomah has started all three games this season, he has played just 47 percent of the defensive snaps.

Anudike-Uzomah is unlikely to stick in Kansas City beyond this season, so getting something in return for him now would be sensible. It would also potentially open more playing time for rookie second-round pick R Mason Thomas .

The Las Vegas Raiders have been arguably the league's biggest surprise this season. This is the main reason that Maxx Crosby isn't a sensible trade chip, even if the Raiders did try to deal him in the offseason.

Las Vegas enters Week 4 with an undefeated record, and quarterback Kirk Cousins is playing well enough that there have been no calls for rookie No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza .

There's a chance that Mendoza doesn't see the field at all as a rookie, though he's certainly the Raiders' future at quarterback. Third-string quarterback Aidan O'Connell, who will be a free agent in 2027, may not be part of Las Vegas' future.

The 2023 fourth-round pick out of Purdue has gotten opportunities to play with the Raiders over the years. He's gone 7-10 as the starter with a career 84.1 QB rating. O'Connell is better than a lot of other backups out there, and with quarterback injuries already mounting, he might be better than a couple of starters.

We've already seen Jaxson Dart, Caleb Williams, Jayden Daniels, and Baker Mayfield suffer fairly significant injuries in 2026. Las Vegas could potentially take advantage by moving O'Connell.

Future Hall of Fame pass-rusher Khalil Mack signed a one-year, $18 million deal to return to the Los Angeles Chargers in free agency. However, the 35-year-old probably didn't think he was signing up for a lost season.

The season isn't lost for the Chargers yet, but at 0-3, they appear to be trending in that direction. If Los Angeles decides to shake up its roster, Mack would be a huge trade asset.

While the Chargers' defense has been uncharacteristically unreliable this season, Mack has already logged two sacks, four tackles for loss, and seven quarterback pressures this season.

Pass-rushers are always in demand in the NFL, and injuries to standouts like Myles Garrett and Brian Burns have only increased the trade value of veterans like Mack.

The Los Angeles Rams entered the regular season as the early Super Bowl favorites. However, they're sitting at just 1-2 after three weeks and are desperate to turn their season around.

General manager Les Snead probably won't even consider selling off important players. He's traditionally been an aggressive buyer on the trade market, and he's certainly been aggressive in 2026.

If the Rams hope to add talent, though, they might consider moving tight end Colby Parkinson as part of a package to get it. The 2024 free-agent addition has been a solid contributor for L.A. over the past couple of seasons, and he has started all three games in 2026. However, he's set to be a free agent in 2027, and the Rams have a surplus of players at tight end.

Parkinson (knee) and fellow tight end Terrance Ferguson (ankle) are both battling injuries, but the Rams also have Tyler Higbee, Davis Allen, and rookie second-round pick Max Klare on the roster.

The Dolphins are in the early stages of a rebuild and parted with most of their marquee veterans during the offseason. Miami had the league's youngest Week 1 roster , and its highest-profile remaining veteran, De'Von Achane, just landed on injured reserve with a torn ACL.

In other words, the Dolphins are short on logical trade chips, though they have one in edge-defender Josh Uche.

Uche joined the Dolphins on a one-year deal and probably isn't in Miami's long-term plans. However, he should have value to another team as a rotational player. He's still only 28 years old, has played 56 percent of Miami's defensive snaps this season, and has recorded 11 tackles and one tackle for loss.

Back in 2022, Uche recorded 11.5 with the New England Patriots.

Former Cincinnati linebacker Ivan Pace Jr. joined the Minnesota Vikings as an undrafted free agent in 2023, and he quickly made an impact on their defense. He appeared in all 17 games as a rookie, made 11 starts, and finished with 102 tackles and 2.5 sacks.

While Pace was also a prominent contributor in his second season, he's slowly fallen out of the defensive game plan. He made just six starts in 2025, and he's only occasionally seen the field this season.

Pace has appeared in all three games but has played nearly twice as many special-teams snaps ( 76 ) as defensive snaps (40).

Keeping Pace as depth in Brian Flores' defense would make some sense. However, he's playing on a one-year deal, and Minnesota could save more than $3 million by trading him. Pace should draw some interest from teams in need of linebacker help.

The Patriots are the defending AFC champions, but at 1-2, they're not exactly where they expected to be after three weeks. New England now finds itself trying to balance the current season and its future.

Rookie first-round pick Caleb Lomu is expected to be a big part of New England's future. Lomu projects as the Patriots' long-term right tackle, and he got the chance to replace starter Morgan Moses in Week 3. Head coach Mike Vrabel told reporters that Moses wasn't benched because his job is in jeopardy.

"Not that I'm aware of," Vrabel said, per Matt Legros of Patriots Wire.

Still, Moses is 35 years old and could be a cap casualty in the offseason—New England would save $9 million in cap space by releasing or trading him next year.

Experienced offensive linemen usually have trade value, and the Patriots could potentially flip Moses for a return while getting Lomu more playing opportunities.

The New Orleans Saints have lost two of their first three games by slim margins. While their 1-2 record is disappointing, the play of second-year quarterback Tyler Shough has been anything but.

Shough hasn't been perfect, but he's shown tremendous growth as a signal-caller. He's already thrown for 917 yards, eight touchdowns, and a 99.2 quarterback rating.

With Shough entrenched as New Orleans' quarterback of the future, the Saints could afford to part with backup Spencer Rattler or third quarterback Zach Wilson. Neither Rattler nor Wilson has had much success as an NFL starter, but both have untapped potential, and Rattler is still on a rookie contract.

According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , Rattler already generated some trade interest during the preseason.

To be clear, pass-rusher Kayvon Thibodeaux is probably the New York Giants' most valuable trade chip. The 2022 first-round pick isn't near the top of New York's edge-rushing rotation, and he's set to be a free agent in 2027.

With Brian Burns now on injured reserve with a torn ACL, though, Trading Thibodeaux at 2-1 doesn't seem all that sensible.

Moving cornerback Deonte Banks, however, would be logical. The 2023 first-round pick has not established himself as a reliable starter, and he'll also be a free agent in 2027, as New York declined his fifth-year option.

Banks did show a little promise under new head coach John Harebaugh in the Giants' season opener. However, he's since been sidelined by a calf injury, and the defense hasn't really missed him.

Banks has allowed a career opposing passer rating of 104.2 in coverage. While he has struggled in New York, though, he's still a former first-rounder at a premium position who should interest other teams.

The New York Jets fell to 1-2 in Week 3, but they've been more competitive than many expected. They're also getting a good look at young offensive pieces like second-year offensive tackle Armand Membou and rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq as they prepare to target quarterbacks in 2027.

One offensive player the Jets could probably part with, though, is offensive tackle Chukwuma Okorafor. The 29-year-old is playing on a one-year deal and is a pure depth piece in New York. While he has appeared in all three games this season, he has played exclusively on special teams—and he's played only 11 total snaps.

While Okorafor is strictly a backup with little long-term value to the Jets, he could potentially aid teams with greater needs along the offensive line. A former starter for the Pittsburgh Steelers, he has 95 regular-season appearances and 60 starts on his resume.

Defensive tackle Moro Ojomo continues to be an integral piece of the Philadelphia Eagles' defensive front. The 25-year-old recorded six sacks and 12 quarterback hits last season, and he has played a career-high 67 percent of the defensive snaps through the first three weeks of 2026.

Under different circumstances, the Eagles probably wouldn't even consider moving a player like Ojomo. What makes Philly's situation unique is the fact that it has already locked up defensive tackles Jordan Davis and Jalen Carter with lucrative second contracts.

There's a very good chance that the Eagles can't justify paying three interior defenders salaries that approach the top of the market. With Ojomo set to be a free agent in 2027, moving Ojomo before the trade deadline would make plenty of sense if the Eagles don't plan to retain him.

Good defensive tackles command a premium, and Philadelphia could expect a strong return for one just entering his playing prime.

Barring an injury, Pittsburgh won't be turning to its QB depth any time soon—and the Steelers have a fair bit of QB depth. Pittsburgh carried four quarterbacks into the regular season, with Mason Rudolph, Will Howard, and rookie Drew Allar sitting behind starter Aaron Rodgers.

According to NFL reporter La Canfora of Casino.org, the Steelers were open to trading Rudolph at the beginning of the year, though there wasn't much demand for journeyman backups. Injuries at the position have probably increased the value of experienced QBs like Rudolph, but Howard might actually be the more sensible trade chip for the Steelers right now.

Rudolph has made 19 career starts and has an 8-5-1 record with Pittsburgh. He's probably the Steelers' best option if Rodgers is forced to miss a game or two. Howard, meanwhile, is a second-year quarterback, and it's hard to envision both he and Allar having a long-term future in Pittsburgh.

Howard is unproven, but he should interest teams in need of a young developmental quarterback.

The San Francisco 49ers are undefeated but already dealing with multiple injuries. They probably aren't interested in moving any current contributors, and they would be wise to hang onto backup quarterback Mac Jones for the time being.

The 49ers were open to moving Jones for a second-round pick in the spring, according to The Athletic's Zack Rosenblatt . However, they may have a real shot at the Super Bowl this year. After watching quarterbacks like Jayden Daniels, Jaxson Dart, Sam Darnold, and Baker Mayfield go down, they may prefer to keep the understudy QB who went 5-3 for them last season.

If Jones' value keeps going up closer to the deadline, things may change. However, San Francisco's most sensible trade assets at this point in the season are draft picks and wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk.

Since we're focusing on players here, we'll highlight Aiyuk, a player who hasn't played since 2024 and one the 49ers have literally begged other teams to come get.

Aiyuk wouldn't bring a big return, but he's not helping San Francisco at all by sitting at home.

The Seattle Seahawks are the defending champs, and they're looking to make another deep run in 2026. After parting with key contributors like Kenneth Walker III, Riq Woolen, and Boye Mafe in the offseason, Seattle shouldn't be interested in losing any more standout players.

However, Seattle could potentially find some value by trading third-string quarterback and 2025 third-round pick Jalen Milroe. He's firmly behind Sam Darnold and Drew Lock on the depth chart, but he's still a very intriguing developmental prospect.

"NFL decision-makers will be more than intrigued about placing him in their offense and building around his skillset," Dame Parson wrote for the Bleacher Report Scouting Department last offseason.

With Darnold delivering a Super Bowl last season and Lock already proving himself to be more than capable as a spot-starter, Milroe is unlikely to see the field in Seattle any time soon. If the Seahawks are going to trade anyone right now, it should be a player they're not using.

A return to the playoffs may simply not be in the cards for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers this season. Tampa sits at 0-3 and will be without starting quarterback Baker Mayfield for at least three weeks because of a dislocated thumb.

The Bucs planned on being firmly in the NFC South mix this season and signed running back Kenny Gainwell to a two-year, $14 million deal in order to flesh out their backfield. However, Gainwell has barely seen the field behind starter Bucky Irving, and if Tampa can't climb back into the playoff picture, he could have much more value to a team with an injured starter.

Gainwell has played just 42 percent of Tampa's offensive snaps and logged a mere 16 touches through three weeks. Meanwhile, we've seen running backs like De'Von Achane, Travis Etienne Jr., Breece Hall, and Jordan Mason suffer injuries.

Last season with the Steelers, Gainwell tallied 1,023 scrimmage yards and eight touchdowns.

The Tennessee Titans are 0-3, and they don't appear to be close to turning around their season. It would behoove the Titans to consider moving any and all expendable veterans in order to bank draft capital and put future pieces around quarterback Cam Ward.

Defensive lineman Solomon Thomas is an expendable veteran for the Titans. Thomas played under head coach Robert Saleh with the Jets, and bringing him in made some sense. However, he simply hasn't been a significant piece of the defensive rotation this season.

Thomas has recorded just four tackles while playing just 26 percent of the defensive snaps. He's set to be a free agent in the spring, and he'd be far more value to a team that has a shot at the postseason in 2026.

The Washington Commanders may have salvaged their season by beating the defending champion Seahawks in Week 3. Things were certainly looking dire before that game, as Washington started 0-2 and lost quarterback Jayden Daniels to a dislocated elbow.

Now, the Commanders have to believe that they can at least stay competitive with Marcus Mariota at quarterback while Daniels recovers. However, they may also have to put some thought into moving defensive tackle Daron Payne.

Interior defensive linemen are an ascending NFL commodity, and Payne has been well above average throughout his career. He has started all three games this season and has tallied four tackles and nine quarterback pressures.

While Washington can certainly use Payne in their defense now, the 29-year-old will be a free agent in the spring and may hold more long-term value as a trade candidate.

*Contract and cap information via Spotrac . Advanced statistics from Pro Football Reference .

articles.title: Travis Kelce’s NFL future gets an intriguing twist as former Patriots veteran points to a factor that could keep the Kansas City Chiefs star playing beyond 2026
articles.summary: Travis Kelce entered the 2026 season with retirement questions around him.
articles.body: Travis Kelce entered the 2026 season with retirement questions around him. Three weeks into his 14th NFL season, though, a new reason has entered the conversation. Rob Gronkowski believes a run at his career touchdown total could give Kelce another reason to return in 2027.The intriguing idea came from Gronkowski himself. During an appearance on the Up & Adams Show with Kay Adams, the former Tampa Bay Buccaneers tight end looked at Kelce’s chase of his 92 career receiving touchdowns. Kelce started 2026 with 82, leaving him 10 behind Gronkowski.Rob Gronkowski sees a record chase keeping Travis Kelce in Kansas CityGronkowski did not say Kelce has decided to play beyond 2026. Instead, he pointed to a scenario that could make another season tempting. “If he gets to that level of touchdowns this year, that would be pretty insane. He would I think he would have to stick around again next year,” Gronkowski said on the “Up & Adams Show.”.The numbers give Kelce a realistic target. He had 82 receiving touchdowns entering the season and needed 10 more to match Gronkowski’s 92. However, Gronkowski’s mark does not stand as the overall tight end record. Antonio Gates owns that record with 116, while Tony Gonzalez sits second with 111.Kelce also has plenty of other milestones already building around his 2026 campaign. Through three games, he had 1,094 career receptions, 13,233 receiving yards and 84 receiving touchdowns. He moved into second place among tight ends in career receiving yards, behind Gonzalez.That gives the retirement story another layer. Kelce does not need to announce anything now. But if he reaches Gronkowski’s number, the possibility of walking away immediately could look different.Travis Kelce has already made his 2026 intentions clearTravis Kelce had already pushed back against the idea that he viewed 2026 as a farewell tour.On Sept. 14, ahead of the Chiefs’ season opener against the Denver Broncos, Kelce spoke with ESPN’s Chris Berman in an interview that aired on Good Morning America. He said he still wanted to compete and did not feel ready to move into life after football.“I want to keep playing until the wheels fall off,” Kelce told Berman. He also said he still believed he could compete at a high level and was “not ready” for the next phase beyond football.That stance followed a much less certain message from January. After Kansas City finished the 2025 season at 6-11, Kelce admitted he needed time to decide his future. He eventually returned for a one-year deal and began his 14th NFL season at age 36.Now, Gronkowski has put another possible storyline on the table. Kelce needs eight receiving touchdowns to pass Gronkowski, and 10 to tie him. If he gets there during the 2026 season, the chase could continue into 2027.As of now, Kelce has made no commitment beyond this season. articles.title: Chiefs Star Travis Kelce’s ‘Rejuvenated’ Season Has Trainers Pointing to Taylor Swift
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce is having a strong season in his 14th year, with his 37th birthday just days away. His speed on routes and league-l...
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce is having a strong season in his 14th year, with his 37th birthday just days away. His speed on routes and league-leading production have fans talking about how much sharper he looks on the field.

Trainers point to his offseason training and July marriage to Taylor Swift as key drivers behind his revived form. They say Swift helped motivate him through intense offseason workouts, which they believe have helped the veteran return to form and play at a high level.

Travis Kelce's trainers credit Taylor Swift for vintage renaissance season

Kelce has turned back the clock through three games, leading the NFL with 155 yards after the catch. He has caught 14 passes for 231 yards and two touchdowns, averaging 16.5 yards per catch during Kansas City's 3-0 start. His average route speed sits at 11.68 mph, his fastest mark since 2022, according to NFL Next Gen Stats.

Trainer Tony Villani attributed the turnaround to Kelce's July marriage to Taylor Swift. "We know if you're putting a good woman in your life and cutting out some of the nonsense, you're probably taking care of yourself a little better," Villani said . "Good surroundings create good outcomes," he added.

Fellow trainer Andrew Spruill noted that Kelce returned to his Florida training grind within a week of the wedding. Everyone wants to look good at their wedding, and Spruill believes that gave Kelce extra motivation to work out hard this offseason.

Villani added that Kelce eliminated outside distractions to stay fully committed to his training schedule.

Kelce's production dipped over the past two seasons before surging back early this year, placing him back among the NFL's premier tight ends.

Fans share their excitement over Kelce's renaissance

Many fans reacted with jokes and theories after seeing Kelce's revived burst on the field this season. Most comments pointed straight to his offseason marriage as the turning point.

One fan wrote , "I don't know if Travis Kelce went over to Europe and got stem cells in his joints or what, but the way he's moving looks different. Maybe Paul Rudd told him where the fountain of youth is located."

A Raiders-focused account added , "We don't know what Taylor Swift did to Travis Kelce during this offseason. But Grandpa is completely rejuvenated."

The lighthearted reactions reflect a broader consensus among fans and analysts who credit Swift for sparking Kelce's early-season dominance.

Kansas City carries its 3-0 start and Kelce's revived burst into Week 4 against the Raiders, with the tight end's fountain-of-youth form now central to the team's Super Bowl push.

New England Patriots kicker Andy Borregales' field-goal accuracy has become a concern through three weeks of play this season.

Borregales has made five field goals this season, but his conversion rate has fallen below the standard expected of an NFL kicker at 71.4 percent.

In 2025, Borregales made 27 of 32 field-goal attempts, good for an 84.4 percent success rate. He also showed range and reliability throughout his rookie season, going a perfect 4-for-4 from 50 or more yards out. He had a few kicks that he may have wanted to get back, which impacted his average.

Nevertheless, he provided the Patriots with a dependable option in scoring territory last season and established a promising foundation for his career, all while helping New England reach the Super Bowl at the end of that season.

Borregales appeared to be primed to take another step forward entering this season. Instead, his early results have not yet reflected that anticipated progression.

The season remains young, and Borregales still has ample time to correct course. Still, the Patriots will need greater accuracy from him as they seek to avoid leaving valuable points on the field for the rest of the season.

articles.body:
Paige Bueckers broke down in tears after the Dallas Wings lost 77-73 to the Golden State Valkyries in Game 3 of their first-round series Friday at Chase Center. The loss eliminated the No. 7 seed from the postseason after Dallas collapsed and blew a 16-point second-half lead. Bueckers had carried the team all year, especially after rookie star Azzi Fudd suffered a season-ending knee injury in August.

She had carried the team all year, especially after rookie star Azzi Fudd suffered a season-ending knee injury in August. However, the two-time WNBA All-Star struggled to find her rhythm from the floor, shooting just 3-of-14 in the deciding game and going completely scoreless in the fourth quarter.

Despite the shooting slump, she finished the night with 17 points, six assists, two steals, and two blocks while going a perfect 10-of-10 at the free-throw line. In the post-game presser, a reporter asked her to reflect on how the Wings completed the best single-season turnaround in WNBA history, improving from a 10-34 record last season to 27-17 this year.

"I think just our selfless nature and how much we enjoyed coming to work," Bueckers answered before pulling the towel over her face as teammate Arike Ogunbowale comforted her, who led Dallas with 30 points.

Bueckers, the top pick in the 2025 WNBA Draft and the reigning Rookie of the Year, made her playoff debut following a difficult 10-34 season for the franchise last year. Under first-year coach Jose Fernandez, Dallas completely transformed, winning a franchise-record 27 games to secure its first postseason appearance since 2023.

Fans react to Paige Bueckers' emotion following season-ending defeat

The emotional clip went viral as fans rallied online to support the young star.

One fan wrote , "She really is a sweetheart & I love her game."

Another added , "I feel for Paige as she's moved to tears… it's easy to forget the human side."

A third fan claimed , "She did so well and shouldn't beat herself up for it."

The fourth noted , "She cared, that's more you can say about a lot of basketball players."

A fifth said , "I love this she going to be even better… She's going to be a monster next season."

The sixth user penned , "I praying for Paige."

Her recent shooting slump also led to some online criticism, but Fernandez addressed the critique directly after the loss. "We only get to this point because of Paige," Fernandez said . "She's a first-team All-WNBA player. She takes ownership in carrying the load. The great ones do."

He noted that she was taking the playoff exit hard, but emphasized that the recent series does not diminish the remarkable season she had for the team.

articles.title: A.J. Brown Injury Update, New Rumors on Patriots WR 'Pushing Hard' to Shorten Return Timeline
articles.summary: As the New England Patriots continue to seek answers for their struggling offense, one thing that could help is A.J. Brown potentially returning as soon as he is eligible to come off injured reserve.
articles.body:
As the New England Patriots continue to seek answers for their struggling offense, one thing that could help is A.J. Brown potentially returning as soon as he is eligible to come off injured reserve.

Per NFL insider Tom Pelissero , Brown is "pushing hard" to be back the first week he is eligible to play in Week 6 against the New York Jets.

The biggest offseason acquisition for New England, Brown played just 31 offensive snaps in Week 1 before suffering an ankle injury against the Seattle Seahawks.

An MRI confirmed Brown's injury was a high-ankle sprain that landed him on IR. The move meant he had to sit out at least the Patriots' next four games.

Typical recovery time from the injury can range from one to six weeks, with a grade 2 sprain taking longer to heal.

Per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , the initial expectation was Brown would likely miss six weeks.

A six-week timeline would keep Brown out through Week 7. He is eligible to be activated off IR and start practicing after the Patriots' game against the Las Vegas Raiders on Oct. 11.

Brown's desire to return as soon as possible comes as the Patriots are trying to avoid falling into an even bigger hole in the AFC. They have lost two of their first three games and will play the undefeated Buffalo Bills on Sunday.

The offense has been a huge problem in New England thus far. The Patriots have yet to score more than 20 points in a game. Drake Maye, who had eight interceptions during the entire 2025 regular season, has thrown an NFL-high six picks through three games this season.

Mack Hollins is the Patriots' leading pass-catcher by receptions (12) and receiving yards (156). No other player on the team has reached double-digits in catches.

articles.title: Bears reportedly expected to start Tyson Bagent at QB in Week 4 vs. Jets
articles.summary: Less than a week removed from leading Chicago to a 'Monday Night Football' victory, Case Keenum will back up Bagent, according to multiple reports.
articles.body:
Despite making a convincing case for why he should continue to serve as the Chicago Bears' starting quarterback while Caleb Williams nurses his hamstring injury , Case Keenum will back up Tyson Bagent on Sunday against the New York Jets, according to multiple reports Saturday .

Bagent, a former undrafted free agent from Division II Shepherd University whom the Bears signed to a two-year extension in August 2025 , will reportedly get the Week 4 start.

Although Ben Johnson lauded Keenum for a prime-time performance in which the 38-year-old turned back the clock , threw for 247 yards and accounted for three touchdowns (one on a QB sneak) in a 27-7 win over the Eagles, the second-year Chicago head coach made it clear there was a reason why Bagent has been Williams' backup .

Keenum started over Bagent in Week 3 because Bagent missed most of the practice week in concussion protocol. The 26-year-old Bagent sustained the injury late in the fourth quarter the previous week amid a 9-3, rain-soaked defeat to the Minnesota Vikings.

At the time, he was replacing Williams, who suffered what's been most recently reported as a Grade 2 hamstring strain that could wind up sidelining him for a month.

Bagent took the majority of first-team reps at practice this week, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport, via ESPN's Saturday report .

Bagent has previously started regular-season games for the Bears. In 2023, while playing for then-head coach Matt Eberflus as a rookie, he made four starts in the place of Justin Fields, who was nursing a thumb injury. Those starts were successive, from Week 7 to Week 10. Bagent led Chicago to a 2-2 record in that span.

That run began with him completing 72.4% of his attempts with one touchdown and no picks in a 30-12 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. Over that four-game stretch, Bagent proved accurate, yet turnover-prone. He posted a 3:5 touchdown-to-interception rate; however, he registered a 65.1% completion rate along the way. Plus, he ran for 105 yards and a score.

It's been more than 1,050 days since Bagent's last regular-season start. Then again, Keenum had about just as long of a drought before his spotlight-stealing outing last Monday.

articles.title: Tyson Bagent Reportedly to Start for Bears vs. Jets Despite Case Keenum's Upset Win vs. Eagles
articles.summary: Despite the feel-good story that resulted from Case Keenum leading the Chicago Bears to a Week 3 win in his first start in three years, Tyson Bagent is expected to be their quarterback on Sunday.
articles.body:
Despite the feel-good story that resulted from Case Keenum leading the Chicago Bears to a Week 3 win in his first start in three years, Tyson Bagent is expected to be their quarterback on Sunday.

Per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport (h/t ESPN's Courtney Cronin ), Bagent is set to start for the Bears against the New York Jets after suffering a concussion in Week 2.

Bagent cleared concussion protocol on Sunday, making him available to play in Monday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles.

However, given the timing, it was easier for the Bears to go with Keenum as their starter since he had received most of the first-team reps during the week of practice.

The move paid off because Keenum was fantastic. He finished 24-of-34 for 247 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions in Chicago's 27-7 victory.

Even though Keenum played well against Philadelphia's defense, signs have been pointing toward Bagent getting the nod in Week 4.

Rapoport noted Bagent received a majority of the first-team reps in practice this week.

Bears head coach Ben Johnson told reporters on Tuesday "there was a reason" Bagent won the backup job coming out of training camp and preseason, though he didn't commit to who his quarterback would be at that time.

Bagent played 10 snaps in the fourth quarter of Chicago's 9-3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings in Week 2. He entered the game after Caleb Williams injured his hamstring on a scramble.

The concussion occurred on the final play of the game when Bagent was sacked by Vikings defensive end Dallas Turner.

Assuming Bagent gets the nod, he will be Chicago's third different starting quarterback in four games. The Bears are off to a 2-1 start going into Sundays matchup with the Jets.

Chicago hasn't opened a season 3-1 since 2020. Bagent, now in his fourth season, has started four games in his NFL career. All four starts came during his rookie year in 2023.

articles.title: Seahawks Owner Vinod Khosla 'Has No Plans' to Relocate Team, Calls Out 'Reporters Looking for Views'
articles.summary: Seattle Seahawks owner Vinod Khosla clarified his recent remarks, making it clear he is not looking to relocate the franchise.
articles.body:
Seattle Seahawks owner Vinod Khosla clarified his recent remarks, making it clear he is not looking to relocate the franchise.

In a post on X, Khosla wrote there are "no plans" to move the Seahawks and blamed the "reporters looking for views" by "distort(ing) my answer out of context" to a question about their future.

49ers Owner Jed York Suspended 6 Games (AP)

Players Who Could Use a Change of Scenery 🏈

The comment being referenced was in an interview Khosla did with Dan Primack of Axios in which he was specifically asked about committing to keeping the Seahawks in Seattle.

"I will never say never," Khosla replied. "Will this team be in Seattle 500 years from now? But I have no current plans to change anything about the team, including the coach, president, operation or Lumen Field. It all functions well."

The Khosla family, including Vinod, his wife Neeru and their son Neal, officially took over as owners of the Seahawks on Sept. 3 when their $9.6 billion purchase of the franchise from Paul Allen's estate closed.

There had been no indications Khosla was exploring a move, but Primack pointed out there was no formal commitment in the purchase agreement to keep the Seahawks in Seattle and asked if he would make that pledge.

This seems like a case of neither side being in the wrong. Primack asked if Khosla would keep the club where they are, and he responded by saying not right now.

The Seahawks' current lease with Lumen Field runs through the 2032 season, but there are options in the deal that could extend it out to 2062.

Given the way that things ended for the SuperSonics in Seattle, you can understand why fans in the city might be a little trepidatious whenever the owner of one of their sports teams leaves open the possibility for relocation.

The Seahawks have been playing in the NFL since 1976. They have reached the Super Bowl four times since the 2005 season, winning in 2013 and 2025.

articles.title: Seahawks' Jadarian Price Placed on IR with Injury, Emanuel Wilson Among Top Waiver-Wire RB Options
articles.summary: Fantasy managers still holding out hope for Seattle Seahawks running back Jadarian Price to turn things around soon will need a backup plan with the rookie going on injured reserve.
articles.body:
Fantasy managers still holding out hope for Seattle Seahawks running back Jadarian Price to turn things around soon will need a backup plan with the rookie going on injured reserve .

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , Price aggravated a chest injury during practice this week that will land him on IR and keep him out for a minimum of four games.

The fantasy impact of Price's absence ensures that Seahawks backup Emanuel Wilson should be a waiver-wire target since he will get the bulk of the carries.

Other potential options that might be available right now include Keaton Mitchell of the Los Angeles Chargers and Alvin Kamara of the New Orleans Saints.

Per Fantasy Pros , all three of Wilson, Mitchell and Kamara are rostered in under 60 percent of PPR leagues. Wilson and Mitchell are both available in more than 65 percent of leagues.

Price, the Seahawks' first-round pick in the 2026 draft, was expected to replace some of the production lost when Kenneth Walker III signed with the Kansas City Chiefs as a free agent.

Things have not worked out as planned thus far. Price has 119 rushing yards on 28 carries, but his playing time has decreased every week in part due to ball-security issues. He has lost a fumble in each of the past two games.

Wilson had already surpassed Price on Seattle's depth chart based on his 32 carries. His efficiency has left a lot to be desired with 3.4 yards per attempt and a 40.6 percent success rate.

Mitchell is in a similar position as Wilson in that his playing time has already started to increase because the original starter was not performing well.

Omarion Hampton is far from the only problem with the Chargers offense, but he's not helping with 3.9 yards per attempt on 50 carries.

Mitchell played a season-high 26 offensive snaps in Week 3 against the Buffalo Bills. He had 13 touches between his carries, receptions and kickoff returns.

The Chargers are using Mitchell more than Hampton in the passing game, too. Mitchell has four catches on four targets, compared to two catches on three targets for Hampton.

Mitchell faces a tough task against the Seahawks on Sunday. After that, though, the Chargers will face the Denver Broncos and Kansas City Chiefs. Those two teams rank in the bottom half of the NFL on defense by EPA per rush, with Denver last in that category.

Kamara is the hardest player from this trio to find since he is rostered in 59.5 percent of leagues right now. His stock went up on Thursday when the Saints put Travis Etienne Jr. on injured reserve due to a hamstring injury.

The issue with Kamara is efficiency is no longer his strong suit, but volume should help him make up for it. He has 24 touches in two games.

New Orleans runs more offensive plays per game than any team in the league, giving Kamara ample opportunity to rack up yards.

articles.title: One NFL analyst believes J.J. McCarthy needs a 'sequence of luck'
articles.summary: This NFL analyst doesn't appear to have much confidence in J.J. McCarthy's future.
articles.body:
J.J. McCarthy's tenure with the Minnesota Vikings was rocky, to say the least. He missed his first full season with a knee injury, lost a training-camp battle to Kyler Murray, was demoted to QB3 on the depth chart, and was traded to the New York Giants , all while on his rookie deal. He could find success outside of Minnesota, but one NFL analyst believes he's going to need a lot of luck.

Sam Monson and Steve Palazzolo of the Check the Mic podcast believe that McCarthy will need a series of fortunate events to find success in the NFL:

"JJ McCarthy is now in a situation where he needs a Geno Smith sequence of lucky things to happen for him to ever get another opportunity."

This is likely the case for McCarthy. Yes, the Giants took a chance on him, but he is viewed as the backup to the backup- nothing more. If this is meant to be a reclamation project for John Harbaugh, that's great. Good luck. But if the expectation is to get quality backup play out of McCarthy, they may be sorely mistaken. The league may pass the former 10th overall pick by, should a sequence of lucky events not transpire.

articles.title: Odell Beckham Jr. earns praise from Giants teammates following release
articles.summary: Odell Beckham Jr.’s Giants reunion ended after 3 games, but teammates praised his legacy and future potential. He now enters free agency after recording no c...
articles.body:
Odell Beckham Jr.'s second stint with the New York Giants ended much sooner than expected, but the veteran wide receiver left the organization with plenty of respect from the players around him. After the Giants released Beckham on Tuesday, several teammates quickly expressed their support for the former Pro Bowler.

Beckham returned to New York this offseason after sitting out the entire 2025 season following a 6-game suspension for a performance-enhancing drug violation and never signing with a team. The 33-year-old earned a spot on the Giants' initial 53-man roster after an encouraging preseason, but his opportunities during the regular season were extremely limited.

Despite not recording a catch through 3 games, Beckham remained highly regarded inside the locker room. Giants players described him as a legend and expressed confidence that he could still find an opportunity elsewhere in the league.

Beckham receives strong support from teammates

Kayvon Thibodeaux was among the Giants players who reacted to Beckham's departure. The edge rusher wished the veteran receiver well and emphasized Beckham's accomplishments throughout his career.

Thibodeaux also pointed to the work Beckham put in to return to the NFL after missing the 2025 season. He said Beckham is capable of making an impact elsewhere, reflecting the respect he still commands from his teammates.

Isaiah Likely offered a similarly supportive message. Likely has an especially strong connection with Beckham because the two previously played together with the Baltimore Ravens in 2023 before reuniting with the Giants.

Beckham's return to New York carried plenty of nostalgia because the Giants originally selected him with the No. 12 overall pick in the 2014 NFL Draft. He immediately became one of the league's most recognizable young stars.

During his first 5 seasons with the Giants, Beckham recorded 390 receptions for 5,476 yards and 44 touchdowns. He also earned 3 consecutive Pro Bowl selections and won Offensive Rookie of the Year in 2014.

His second stint looked very different. Beckham played about 20 offensive snaps, roughly 10–11% of the team's offensive plays, through 3 games and received just 1 target, failing to record a reception before the Giants decided to move on.

The Giants did not simply give Beckham a place on the roster because of his history with the organization. Head coach John Harbaugh said before the season that Beckham had earned his position after showing he could still contribute.

Beckham recorded multiple catches in the preseason, including 7 catches for 76 yards across preseason games, which helped him secure one of the limited receiver spots on the final roster. Harbaugh praised his overall performance and said he had demonstrated that he was ready to help the team.

The problem was finding consistent opportunities once the regular season began. Malik Nabers, Darnell Mooney and rookie Malachi Fields were ahead of Beckham in the receiving rotation, while injuries and other roster changes also affected how the Giants constructed their offense.

Fun fact: Beckham became the first Giants player to record 3 consecutive seasons with at least 1,300 receiving yards, reaching the mark in 2014, 2015, and 2016.

Beckham's lack of playing time became increasingly difficult to justify as the Giants adjusted their roster. He appeared on only 20 of the team's 191 offensive snaps through 3 games, or roughly 10.5% of the total.

His only target came during the Giants' Week 3 victory over the Tennessee Titans. Beckham did not catch the pass, meaning his return to the team ended without an official reception.

The Giants subsequently promoted return specialist Braxton Berrios from the practice squad to the active roster. Because Berrios had already used his 3 practice-squad elevations, New York needed to create an active-roster spot, and Beckham was released. The team also added receiver Charlie Jones from the practice squad in the same move.

His NFL career still has another chapter

Beckham is now a free agent again and can explore opportunities with other teams. His recent lack of production is part of the story, but his larger career record gives teams plenty of history to consider.

Across 122 career regular-season games, Beckham has recorded 575 receptions for 7,987 yards and 59 touchdowns. He has also played for the Cleveland Browns, Los Angeles Rams, Baltimore Ravens and Miami Dolphins and won Super Bowl LVI with the Rams.

His teammates clearly believe there is still something left for him to contribute. Thibodeaux said Beckham would be able to make a statement somewhere, while Likely expressed hope that Beckham would continue to do what he has done throughout his career.

Fun fact: Beckham averaged 108.8 receiving yards per game during his 2014 rookie season, the highest mark by a rookie receiver in NFL history.

Beckham leaves Giants with lasting legacy

Although this reunion lasted only 3 games, Beckham's connection to the Giants remains significant. His spectacular rookie season and memorable one-handed touchdown catch helped establish him as one of the defining young stars of his era.

His first Giants tenure also produced some of the strongest statistical seasons of his career. Before leaving New York in 2019, Beckham had already established himself as one of the franchise's most recognizable offensive players.

That history helps explain why his release generated such a strong reaction inside the locker room. Even without a catch during his latest stint, Beckham remained someone his teammates respected for his career, persistence, and influence.

The Giants will now move forward without Beckham as they prepare for their next game against the Arizona Cardinals. The roster change comes during a busy stretch for New York, which has also made significant moves at quarterback.

The team recently acquired J.J. McCarthy from Minnesota in exchange for a 2027 fifth-round pick. John Harbaugh has said Jameis Winston will start against Arizona, while the team had not publicly confirmed whether McCarthy or Jake Haener would serve as the backup.

For Beckham, the next step will be finding a situation that offers a larger role than the one he received in New York. His Giants teammates have already made clear that they believe his story in the NFL is not finished.

Odell Beckham Jr. was released by the Giants after 3 games and no receptions during his second stint with the franchise.

Kayvon Thibodeaux and Isaiah Likely publicly praised Beckham and expressed confidence that he can make an impact elsewhere.

Beckham earned his roster spot after an encouraging preseason but played only 20 offensive snaps during the regular season.

The veteran receiver remains a major part of Giants history after starring for the team during his first 5 seasons.

Beckham is now a free agent looking for another opportunity after previously winning a Super Bowl with the Rams.

articles.title: Bart Scott says CBS treated him ‘like a puppet’ during Ray Rice scandal: ‘Tried to pit me against him’
articles.summary: Like many outspoken NFL athletes before and since, former New York Jets linebacker Bart Scott had a meteoric rise in sports media after retiring from the lea...
articles.body:
Like many outspoken NFL athletes before and since, former New York Jets linebacker Bart Scott had a meteoric rise in sports media after retiring from the league.

Scott, who was the face of a New York defense that made it to two straight AFC title games, was elevated to a full-time role on The NFL Today at CBS in 2014. That same season, NFL coverage was dominated by the Ray Rice domestic violence story.

So in his first season in a major media seat, Scott was forced to weigh in on a generational scandal involving one of his former teammates. Scott even got the call-up to CBS This Morning to give his reaction to Rice's two-game suspension. In an interview this week on The Pivot , Scott recalled feeling that CBS "tried to pit me against him" and that the network was using him "like a puppet" to get a clip of a fellow NFL player criticizing Rice.

"One thing I hated about my experience with CBS … I felt like they thought they were going to use me like a puppet, and I reversed, Uno, draw-two, f*ck you," he said.

"What they wanted was crazy, can't wait, can't believe this, ahh 'He beat his wife, he should be banned, blah, blah, blah.' Right? And they wanted that, and I can tell that they were setting me up for that. But if they would have did their opposition research, they would have known that I was a teammate of Ray. They knew that I was a teammate, but some guys that was his teammate … didn't hold in and lock in.

"This is the type of friend I am. And I f*ck with Ray, we all f*ck with Ray. But I'm the type of friend when the world is against you, even though I would be against you, I'm gonna support you and then I'm going to be against you and take you to the side after the fact. After I help you through the storm. I ain't gonna abandon you, you know what I'm saying? I'm going to walk you through the storm and then say, 'Man, what you did, I can't rock with that.'"

In a CBS This Morning interview (still available on YouTube ), Scott explained that Rice's situation was fairly unprecedented . Rather than agreeing Rice got off easy , Scott suggested the incident might lead to formalized rules around domestic violence suspensions.

One of the show's anchors asked Scott directly whether he had spoken with Rice. Scott confirmed he had, and cited Rice's "tremendous record" prior to the video showing him striking his then-fianceé. Clearly beneath the surface, Scott had mixed feelings about the setup.

"They wanted me to throw Ray underneath the bus and step on him and build it so they could have these big clips. And I refused," he explained on The Pivot .

"Because I'm a believer that no man should be judged by his worst moment, right? So that was his worst moment. And what I'm also not gonna do is I'm not gonna pile on when the world's piling on. And you have to ask yourself, when somebody does something bad, is this a bad person doing a bad thing? Or is this a good person that had a bad moment?

"And I knew that Ray Rice was a good person that had a bad moment, which we all can do impulsive things … we shouldn't be defined by that. And I hated that the industry tried to pit me against him and try to use me for clickbait. And I refused to do it. And I could tell; I could look at her face when she was trying to get out of me what she wanted to get out of me.

"I've been around the game too long, too savvy, been around these crazy-a** reporters that try and get you, especially in New York, they try and get you to say sh*t and use their journalistic tricks that don't work on me. Because I'm not some Neanderthal, right? To this day, I think that Ray Rice has lived his apology."

Scott shared on The Pivot that when he left for the Jets, Rice took over his Baltimore-area charity helping victims of addiction. More recent coverage of Rice has shown that he and his partner remained together and continued to build a family after the incident, and that Rice has become a speaker and advocate against domestic violence in sports.

When sports stories become national news, outlets often interview athletes as experts. However, the backgrounds and relationships these athletes carry are different from the cozy ties of the political world. As Scott shared, it was clear CBS knew he had a relationship with Rice, yet expected him to shred it to make good television.

"They set us up, but they don't care about the relationship that they could have ruined between me and Ray Rice," Scott said. "They just want to use me as a puppet."

In the end, the legacy of the Rice story became just as much about sports media as the NFL. The situation laid bare many reporters' deference to the league office , and the industry's discomfort in addressing domestic violence .
